subject: In 1,700 adults, frequent midlife TV tracked smaller memory regions
script: From Agewell Brief: In 1,700 adults, frequent midlife TV tracked smaller memory regions. A new study of 1,700 adults finds that frequent TV viewing in midlife is associated with smaller brain regions and more white matter damage in later years. Frequent TV viewers showed smaller memory and decision-making brain areas. White matter damage was more common in heavy TV watchers. Read the full source-linked dispatch and primary study caveats at AgewellBrief.com.
